# Slow Extraction, Deep Grace

## Scripture

"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law." — Galatians 5:22–23

## Reflection

Good pour-over coffee cannot be rushed. Pour the water too fast and it channels straight through the grounds, leaving a thin, sour cup. The richest flavor comes from a slow, steady pour—water meeting grounds, patience doing its quiet work.

Paul describes the fruit of the Spirit the same way: not a microwave result but a slow extraction. Love, joy, peace, patience—these are not pressed into us in a moment. They seep out over time as we stay under the steady pour of God's Word, prayer, and ordinary obedience. The roasting is not comfortable. Heat and pressure draw out what is hidden, and so do hard seasons. Yet the Lord is not impatient with the process. He tends the brew.

Our part is not to force flavor but to remain in the grounds—to keep showing up in the small, unglamorous rituals: a morning verse before the phone, a whispered prayer in traffic, a kind word when we are tired. Character forms in the drip, not the downpour. When we are tempted to hurry our own growth, remember that the Father is a patient roaster and a careful barista. He knows exactly how long the extraction needs. Let today's slow cup remind you: grace is never instant, but it is always worth the wait.

## Prayer

Father, keep us patient in the slow work of becoming like Jesus. Pour Your Spirit over us steadily, and let the fruit You grow in us bless everyone who tastes our lives. In Christ's name, amen.

## One-Line Application

Stay under the slow pour; let God extract His fruit in you.
